reasoning: Set A fits the stated project better. It has one shared core where every environment and both learner families go through a single train_run loop. It stays on free tools, carries the concepts the user wants to study through all three stages (ablation switches on exploration, memory and the frozen copy; a REINFORCE → actor-critic → PPO ladder; turns, simultaneous and self-play schedules with a cross-play table), and the spec's numbers are worked through and correct (returns 1.99/1/0, energy 0.798). Its roadmap gives each stage the same three-milestone shape (train, then baselines/curves/replay, then study), and each milestone depends on the one before for a real reason. A's weaknesses are size and stale text. The PL-01 step table has 34 rows covering every stage's environments, it is not in call order, and it is repeated in full in every context packet. The architecture still contains process narration ('M1 has 0 of 22 tasks done', 'the build waits for … replan'), and the brief still says 'the second environment, whatever it is'. The four DQN thicken tasks are chained one after another even though the interface split them so each writes its own file. Set B is tighter and easier to read, and its first milestone is a better walking skeleton because it includes the replay. But it departs from the user's ground truth in several ways: it allows a paid cloud GPU (QR-02, AD-09), it has no shared training loop (train_dqn and train_ppo each run their own), and it adds a sign-off gate that training must pass. Its roadmap is lopsided: M3 and M4 are each a whole stage, M3 lists 7 pipelines, there is no walking skeleton for the fish tank or predator-prey stages, and M3/M4 lack Skills and References lines. It also contradicts itself in places: train_ppo runs 'until the time limit' while AD-18 makes the step budget the stop rule, and the pipelines defer to the null-hypothesis-testing and dataviz skills that AD-14/AD-20/AD-21 say are a placeholder and not installed.

Toy test environments (corridor, line, chase) prove the core with no changes to it

Stale process narration in the architecture and a stale line in the brief
False serialization of the four DQN thicken tasks, which each write their own file
Task IDs run out of order (T20–T24 come before T14)
M1 can't be watched; replay only arrives in M2
